title: Customizing Graph Neural Network for CAD Assembly Recommendation

problem.claim: CAD assembly recommendation aims to help designers select the next required component from existing components and speed up the design process.

gap.claim: Existing CAD assembly recommender systems use fixed GNN architectures that may be sub-optimal for manufacturers with different data distributions.

contributions.claim: CusGNN is a neural architecture search framework for automatically designing data-specific GNNs for different manufacturers.
The framework defines a search space across aggregation, fusion, and readout functions and uses a differentiable search algorithm to identify high-performing GNNs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CusGNN as a novel neural architecture search framework for CAD assembly recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that customized GNNs achieve 1.5–5.1% higher top-10 accuracy than previous manually designed methods.
The authors report that code and data are available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: CAD assembly modeling uses existing machine-component catalogs to support industrial product design, and GNN recommenders can assist component selection.
Fixed GNN architectures may not suit manufacturers with different data distributions.
CusGNN searches for manufacturer-specific GNNs using a three-dimensional search space and differentiable search.
The authors report higher top-10 accuracy for customized GNNs than previous manually designed methods.
The authors state that code and data are available.

source_observation.claim: Fixed GNN architectures may be sub-optimal when manufacturers have different data distributions.

interpretation.claim: Model architecture selection may need to account for distribution-specific variation rather than rely on a single fixed design.

application.claim: For heterogeneous manufacturing settings, evaluate automated or adaptive architecture selection for each data environment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when customized architecture search is preferable to a fixed architecture or how its costs compare.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the manufacturers, datasets, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not report absolute accuracy values, statistical significance, or search and training costs.
The abstract does not detail the searched operations or the differentiable search algorithm.
